summary: 40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab built 1936 on Washington Butte near Pateros; removed in 1952. A 2020 visit found the old summit road now a trail.

facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1952; a June 2020 visit found no tower, only the old summit road, now a trail

access.note: On Wenatchee National Forest land; Forest roads reach the area and usually open in spring after the snow melts. The last part is a walk.

visit.trail_note: Old road from the saddle to the summit is now a trail: about a quarter mile with roughly 200 feet of climb, per Willhite's 2020 visit

events.note: Tower removed; both the register and Willhite give 1952

evidence.supports: built 1936 as a 40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab, removed 1952

notes_for_editor: The 1936 build and 1952 removal agree across all three sources. The 40 ft versus 52 ft height gap is unresolved (the register's 40 ft pole tower against Willhite's 1938 roof-height photographs at 52 ft); the story says so and no height_m is given. No staffing, fire or use history was found; a second search returned nothing usable. Willhite's 'Remaining relic' photo has a second caption line, 'Maybe a metal jug', which is a guess; no source confirms the object. Access is marked public because the site is on National Forest land; no source states that directly.
